title: performance: canary regression detection + rollout guards (adaptive thresholds, KV-aware hysteresis)
author: Ava Chen
description: Add adaptive performance canary regression detection and rollout guards with KV-cache aware hysteresis. Motivation: we observed flaky canary flips driven by transient KV cache warmup and burst traffic leading to noisy latency regressions that caused unnecessary rollbacks. This change adds: 1) adaptive thresholding that adjusts latency/throughput baselines using recent distribution percentiles (p50/p95/p99 windowed), 2) hysteresis that is KV-cache-aware (shorter sensitivity during stable cache state, relaxed during warmup), 3) a new rollout_guard config allowing per-model and per-route tuning (min_sample_size, sensitivity, backoff_windows), 4) canary event enrichment for tracing (metrics + span tags) and 5) unit and integration tests plus canary e2e smoke tests. The description below summarizes commits, changed areas, review discussion, CI results, and merge outcome.
commits: feat(perf-canary): add adaptive threshold detector and hysteresis engine
test(perf-canary): add unit tests for adaptive detector
docs(perf-canary): document rollout_guard config and examples
fix(perf-canary): address race in KV warmup detection
chore: version bump and changelog entry
review_threads: Miguel: Can we get more explanation on the percentile window size choice? Ava: Added comment and made window configurable via rollout_guard.window_seconds, default 300s.
Priya: Race in KV warmup detection looked possible in concurrent requests. Ava: fixed by adding an atomic state transition and added tests covering concurrent warmup scenarios.
Jordan: Can this increase memory usage if we keep distribution samples long-term? Ava: we only keep rolling histograms with bounded buckets; documented memory cost and defaults in docs.
Priya: Request small API shape change to rollout_guard (rename sensitivity->sensitivity_pct). Ava: applied rename and added migration note in docs.
ci_checks: unit tests: initially failed (flaky test in adaptive_detector), rerun passed
notes_for_release: Adds adaptive canary detection and rollout guard config. Default behavior is backward compatible. Operators can opt-in and tune sensitivity_pct, min_sample_size, and window_seconds per model/route.
changelog_entry: perf(canary): adaptive thresholding + KV-aware hysteresis for canary rollout guards (ENG-2741) - improves stability of automated rollouts by reducing noise from cache warmups and transient bursts.
testing_notes: Added unit tests for detector and hysteresis logic. Ran local perf harness against small simulated workloads (1000 requests/min) with controlled KV warmup patterns. CI includes an e2e canary job that deploys a canary and validates no false-positive rollbacks in synthetic warmup scenarios.
follow_up: Consider adding ML-backed anomaly scoring if thresholds produce too many misses; tracked in ENG-2800. Monitor memory usage of rolling histograms for high-throughput routes.
human_readable_diff: High-level: added adaptive detector and KV-aware hysteresis. Code changes are confined to services/perf-canary; docs updated. No API breaking changes to external clients. Example snippet: rollout_guard: { min_sample_size: 200, sensitivity_pct: 5, window_seconds: 300 }.
deployment_instructions: Deploy perf-canary service and update config via Console or config repo. Optional per-model rollout_guard overrides can be applied post-deploy. No DB migrations required.
post_deploy_checks: Monitor canary-alerts for 24h, check canary_metrics (canary_regressions, canary_flip_count) and tracing spans for canary.enriched=true. Verify no spike in false-positive rollbacks.
author_notes: This is opt-in for teams; default settings are conservative. We validated on internal staging with typical Redwood traffic patterns. Reach out if you want help tuning for enterprise customers with dedicated caches.
